o.text: From Persian بدبخت (badbaxt). By surface analysis, bəd + bəxt.
. By surface analysis, an irregular derivation from sik (“dick”).

Inherited from Old Anatolian Turkish یازق (yazuq), from Proto-Common Turkic *yāzuk, from Proto-Common Turkic *yāz- (“to err; to make a mistake; to miss out”).
Etymology notes
Cognate with Old Uyghur [script needed] (yazuk), Karakhanid یازُوکْ (yāzuq, “sin”), Kipchak yaxuc (yazuk), Ottoman Turkish یازیق (yazïq, “what a shame”), Gagauz yazık, Turkmen ýazyk (“sin, wrongdoing”), Crimean Tatar yazıq, Kumyk языкъ (yazıq, “pitiable”), Bashkir яҙыҡ (yaðıq, “sin, wrongdoing”), Tatar язык (yazıq, “sin”), Kazakh жазық (jazıq), Uzbek yoziq, Khakas чазых (çazıx), Southern Altai јазык (ǰazïk), Kyrgyz жазык (jazık). Compare also Yakut сыысхал (sïïsqal, “mistake”).
Has been compared to Chuvash ҫылӑх (śylăh, “sin”) which, if really cognate, would warrant a Proto-Turkic reconstruction; the Chuvash word is, however, rather from *yaŋïl, i.e. cognate with Azerbaijani yanlış, yanılmaq, etc.
The Old Turkic 𐰖𐰔‬‬𐰴 (yazïq, “plain, steppe”) is from *yaz- (“to spread out, to lay”), thus unrelated.
For the semantic development of 'sin' → 'sinful' → 'miserable' → 'poor, pitiable', compare the developments in the modern descendants of Old Norse synd (“sin”).
From öpmək (“to kiss”) + -üş. Cognate with Turkish öpüşmek.

o.text: From Proto-Turkic *k(i)amak, *k(i)apak (“forehead; front; part; eyelid; eyebrow”). Cognate with Turkish kabak, Uzbek qovoq (“eyelid”), Khakas хамах (xamax, “forehead”), Bashkir ҡабаҡ (qabaq, “eyelid”) etc.
From bülöv + -lə. Diachronically, the word contains two suffixes -lə, one of which is no longer recognizable.
Calque of Russian замеча́тельный преде́л (zamečátelʹnyj predél).

glosses: kernel (the central (usually edible) part of a nut, especially once the hard shell has been removed)

o.text:
Borrowed from Classical Persian لبه (laba).
Budukh лапа (lapa), Lezgi лепе (lepe) terms were likely introduced by Azerbaijani.
Borrowed from Russian электротехника (elektrotexnika). By surface analysis, elektro- + texnika.
